about: READS the public mirror's check results back onto the publish packet (backlog 321f1409, David 2026-09-19): the machine step `read-checks` of publish-to-github v7. Runs infra/forge/read-publish-checks.sh with no packet-supplied text — the one arg it admits is the literal `--check`, its no-network input check. A run (no arg) finds the one open publish-to-github packet whose read-checks step is ready, takes the PR's head sha and url off its completed open-pr step (the sha publish-github-pr recorded when it pushed, never re-derived), reads GET /repos/algedonic-dev/boss/commits/<head>/check-runs over the PUBLIC API with no credential, waits until the code-scanning check-runs are completed — the CodeQL check and its Analyze (…) jobs, ONLY those since backlog d167e7d7, because the mirror also runs a full infra/gate.sh that can outlast the deadline (Analyze (rust) took 13 minutes on both #238 and #239; the wait is bounded by the script's own deadline, below this timeout, so the packet sees the script's FAILED line naming the run still in flight rather than the runner's kill) — and then, since backlog c6cb678b, completes nothing while ANY check is still running: the partial reading goes on the packet, a running check named in still_running with no conclusion, and the verb answers `not yet` (exit 75) at once, so the runner is never held for the gate; the rule reread-publish-pr-every-15-minutes files this verb again every fifteen minutes until every check has completed, and a check still running four hours after the PR opened completes the step as `unfinished`, naming it. The step's conclusion is the verdict over EVERY check — the scan's own when it did not pass, else `failure` when any other check failed (named in `failing`) — because PR #243 closed pr-opened with its Gate red, recorded in_progress by a read that judged CodeQL alone, reads the CodeQL check-run's annotations (every page the API exposes), PATCHes the reading onto the packet's metadata as `code_scanning` — one entry per check with its conclusion, and for CodeQL the counts by rule, by file and by level — and completes read-checks with conclusion / alerts / rules. Nothing on this host is mutated and nothing on GitHub is written: the only writes are the publish packet's own reading and step, and the merge on GitHub stays David's. Measured before this verb existed: PR #238 was merged over 64 unread alerts (18 critical) on 2026-09-12 and #239 stalled on 109 (10 critical) — 100 of 100 annotations name heuristics (account_id / employee_id / uid in a log line) or #[cfg(test)] constants, and nothing inside BOSS had read either. The dispatcher rule read-publish-checks-on-read-checks-ready files this when open-pr completes; complete-publish-read-checks-on-read-publish-checks-answered reads the answer line and, on a non-zero exit, annotates the step and files the alert. The wait blocks this host's ops-runner for its length (the runner answers serially) — a stated cost, once per publish; the script header names the alternatives and why they were declined. Since backlog 663589cd (David 2026-09-26, PR #244 closed red and alarmed for 22 hours) every run first asks GitHub what became of each publish PR not already read closed — open, merged or closed, the head's checks NOW while it is open, and why when it closed unmerged — and writes it onto that PR's packet as pr_state (infra/forge/publish-pr-state.sh, the pass the daily mirror-drift verb shares), so a close reaches the publish region within the rule's fifteen minutes rather than the next day.
